player.name: Brakka Stonejaw
player.concept: a loud half-orc barbarian with a big axe, a short temper and a secret love of poetry

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Late-afternoon light slants across the crossroads, catching on a weathered milestone and an empty gibbet. A dead ox lies in the ditch, crude arrows jutting from its flank. Crows watch from the blackthorn hedges, where the wind carries a faint smell of woodsmoke.

A mud-caked farmer jabs his pitchfork at the hedge, then shouts at the milestone as if it has answered him. His eyes are bloodshot; his hands shake with exhaustion. Suddenly, he spots you and swings the pitchfork your way. “You—! Stand there! Are you goblins in disguise?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I throw my arms wide and bellow with laughter. "GOBLINS? Do goblins stand seven feet tall and smell this magnificent, little man?" I squint at the milestone. "And what has the stone been saying to you? Did it insult your mother? Point me at it. I will split it in two."

transcript.speaker: tam
transcript.text: *Tam’s pitchfork wavers between Brakka and the milestone. A frightened laugh cracks out of him.* “Don’t you go splitting stones, turnips save us! It ain’t the stone—well, it didn’t say anything. I was shouting at the hedge. There’s little green devils in there, and they killed my ox!” *He jabs the pitchfork at the arrows, then lowers it a fraction.* “You’re… not a goblin, then? You look awful big to be one.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I lean down close to Tam, conspiratorial. "Not a goblin. But I will tell you a secret, farmer: I was raised by goblins. Three winters in a warren under the Blackmoor hills. I speak their tongue like a native." I cup my hands around my tusks and roar at the hedge in a guttural goblin snarl: "OI! SNOTLINGS! COME OUT AND PARLEY! BRAKKA BRINGS CHEESE!"

transcript.speaker: dice
transcript.text: Persuasion check: 10 + 1 = 11 vs DC 10: success

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Your goblin roar rolls down the drovers’ track. For a heartbeat, the hedges give nothing back—then Tam’s pitchfork dips, and he catches your arm as if you’re the first solid thing he’s seen all day.

He spills it in a breathless rush: the ox, the little green devils in the hedges, the toll-house men laughing him away. As he speaks, his free hand keeps drifting to a lump beneath his smock. The crows shift on the gibbet, watching.

transcript.speaker: tam
transcript.text: *Tam grips your arm tighter, then notices and lets go, wiping his palm on his muddy coat.* “You really know their tongue? Saints bless you—then they heard you. They’ve been following me since dawn, ever since they killed my ox on the drovers’ track. Toll-house fools said I’d been at the cider.” *He glances toward the hedge, then down the road.* “Walk me home to Hollis Farm? Bet’s there, an hour down the track. I—I can’t have the little devils follow me to her door.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I nod gravely and clap one huge hand on his shoulder. "Brakka will walk you home, little farmer." With my other hand, as quietly as a seven-foot half-orc can manage, I try to slip my fingers under his smock and lift whatever that lump is he keeps touching.

transcript.speaker: dice
transcript.text: Insight check: 20 + 1 = 21 vs DC 12: success (natural 20!)

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Tam’s eyes flick to your hand before it reaches his smock. He clamps both hands over the hidden lump, and his fear sharpens into embarrassment. “No. That’s mine.”

After a beat, he draws out a small figure carved from pale bone: a hunched grandmother with garnet eyes that catch the dying light. It feels less like a trinket than something meant for a shrine. Tam holds it tight against his chest, jaw set, waiting for your answer.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I raise both hands, palms out. "Peace, peace. Brakka only wanted to look." Then I go very still, staring at those garnet eyes. My voice drops low. "I know her. In the warren the goblins carved her on every wall. The Bone Grandmother. Tam... where did you get this? I do not think they are hunting you. I think they want HER back." Half to myself, I murmur: "Garnet eyes in the gloaming, bone that remembers the hand that carved it..."

transcript.speaker: tam
transcript.text:
*Tam’s grip tightens around the idol. He gives a brittle little laugh, then looks from the garnet eyes to the hedge.* “I found it under my plough, wrapped in rotten leather. Three days ago. I was taking it to Caerwyn to sell—there, I said it. New ox doesn’t buy itself.”

*His pitchfork lowers, just a little.* “If those devils want it back, then maybe… maybe I shouldn’t carry it home to Bet. But I’ve lost enough already, Brakka. You swear they’re after this thing?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I open my mouth to swear... then shut it. I scratch the back of my neck and grin sheepishly. "Swear? No. Brakka cannot swear. Truth is, I made all that up. Never lived in a warren. Never spoke goblin in my life, that was just shouting. My mother kept the archive at the temple of Saint Orrin and taught me to read verse." I shrug enormously. "The cheese part was true, though." I pull a crumbly wedge from my pack and offer it to him. "But it is a good story, yes? And maybe it is even right."

transcript.speaker: tam
transcript.text:
*Tam stares at Brakka, then at the cheese. A frightened little laugh escapes him; he takes the wedge with a shaky hand.* “You made it up? Saints and turnips, I thought you had ’em talking! Well… a good story’s still more than the toll-house gave me.”

*He hugs the idol close, then looks anxiously toward the hedge.* “I don’t know if they want it. But I won’t take it to Bet—not till we know. And I’m not leaving it by the road for those little devils, neither. Help me think, Brakka?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I slap my thigh. "Brakka has a plan! A beautiful plan." I point at the empty gibbet. "We hang your bone grandmother up there, high, like bait. Then I climb inside your dead ox. Whoever comes for her, I burst out of the ox roaring and we see who they are." I am already marching to the ditch, rolling up my sleeves and drawing my knife to open up the carcass. "You hide in the hedge on the other side, Tam. Not that hedge. The other one."

transcript.speaker: tam
transcript.text:
*Tam recoils, clutching the idol to his chest.* “No! Saints preserve us, Brakka—you’re not cutting open my ox! And we’re not hanging her up like bait. What if it brings them straight to us?”

*He glances nervously at the hedges, then lowers his voice.* “We can keep the idol covered and go toward the toll house together. Or… you’ve got that cheese. Could we leave a bit out and watch from the road?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I grumble and sheathe the knife. "Fine. Your ox keeps his guts. Cheese, then. Everyone knows goblins love cheese." I haul myself up the gibbet, wedge the rest of my cheese on the crossbar where it can be seen from both hedges, then drop down and flop into the ditch beside the dead ox, arms out, tongue lolling, playing dead. Out of the side of my mouth: "Tam. Hide. Watch the hedges."

transcript.speaker: tam
transcript.text:
*Tam stares at you sprawled beside the ox, then gives a thin, startled laugh.* “Saints and turnips, that’s a fine way to get pecked. I’m not hiding in either hedge—not with them in there.”

*He tucks the idol beneath his smock and crouches behind the milestone, pitchfork ready.* “I’ll watch from here. And if anything comes for that cheese, Brakka, you’d best be ready to wake up.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I lie perfectly still in the ditch and wait, watching the hedges through slitted eyes, breathing slow. If a crow lands on me, I let it. I wait as long as it takes for something to come for that cheese.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
You lie still in the ditch, the dead ox’s hide cold against your shoulder. A crow lands on your boot, then hops up your shin, pecking once at your trouser seam.

Across the road, Tam’s pitchfork rises behind the milestone. The blackthorn hedge shivers—not with the wind. A wiry figure in a wolf-skin hood steps into the open, one ear missing; four green shapes ghost into view behind him, short bows trained on the crossroads. The leader’s gaze fixes on the cheese atop the gibbet, then snaps to Tam’s smock. He rattles the bones in his hand and points his curved knife at the farmer.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Skrag rattles his bones and points his curved knife at Tam’s smock. He barks a sharp phrase in goblin; the four archers hold their bows trained across the crossroads.

Tam rises behind the milestone, pitchfork shaking but thrust forward. The cheese remains untouched atop the gibbet. The crow on Brakka’s boot flaps away.
